newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Paper - Russian court rules against Smirnoff vodka.
newsitem.headline: Paper - Russian court rules against Smirnoff vodka.

text.p: Russian business paper Kommersant Daily said at the weekend the Moscow Regional Arbitration Court had ruled against the use of the Smirnoff vodka brandname held by Britain's Grand Metropolitan Plc in favour of its Russian rival Smirnov.

The court rejected an earlier appeal by Grandmet's U.S. subsidiary Heublein against the Russian Trademark Chamber decision which cancelled Smirnoff brandname's official registration in Russia two years ago, the newspaper said.
Grandmet in London said it had no comment on the newspaper report.

But the London-listed company, which has appealed against all previous rulings, has said the dispute would have no effect on sales of Smirnoff outside Russia. Heublein sells around 15 million cases of Smirnoff vodka around the world, including one million in Russia.

But Kommersant quoted a lawyer for the Russian firm, P.A. Smirnov and Descendants in Moscow, as saying the court ruling, which was the third negative ruling in a row for Heublein, may lead to a ban on imports of Smirnoff vodka to Russia.

Heublein and certain descendants of Pyotr Smirnov, official supplier of vodka to the Tsar in the last century, have been in dispute since 1992, when Boris Smirnov launched brandname production in Russia and pledged to ban Smirnoff imports, which he said were illicit.
GrandMet says Heublein bought the rights to sell vodka under the Smirnoff name in 1939 from a Russian emigre who had himself acquired them from Pyotr's son Vladimir.
GrandMet is planning a merger with Guinness.
